subject: discrete-mathematics
subtopics: binary operation, closure and the algebraic-structure ladder (semigroup, monoid, group, abelian group)
monoids: identity, uniqueness of the identity, and the standard examples
group axioms, uniqueness of identity and inverse, cancellation and the reversal rule (ab)^-1 = b^-1 a^-1
order of a group and order of an element, and the divisibility corollary
abelian groups and the conditions that force commutativity
subgroups and the one-step and two-step tests
cyclic groups, generators and groups of prime order
cosets, the index and Lagrange's theorem
the small cast of groups GATE reuses: Z_n, direct products, matrix groups, power sets under symmetric difference
permutation groups and the symmetric group

chosen.title: Group theory Notes for GATE Exams
covers: algebraic structures: semigroup, monoid, group, abelian group
group properties: uniqueness of identity and inverse, cancellation, power laws
cyclic groups and subgroups generated by an element
Lagrange's theorem and the divisibility of the subgroup order
chosen.why: The only GATE-oriented written source found whose whole text could be read in this run: it states the ladder, the group properties, the subgroup tests, the cyclic-group definition and Lagrange's theorem in the exact vocabulary GATE uses. Chosen for readability and syllabus fit, not for length; every claim it supplies was recomputed before publication.

chosen.title: Algebraic Structure | Group Theory | Discrete Mathematics | Lecture 01
covers: binary operation and the closure property
monoid as a semigroup with identity
group as a monoid in which every element has an inverse
abelian group as a group with the commutative property
chosen.why: The best explanation found for the ladder in any language: it builds the five rungs in order with a worked example per rung, which is the order a beginner needs. The Hindi auto-captions (Devanagari ASR) were readable for the whole definitions segment. It is the only non-English source used, and every sentence taken from it is translated into English and marked as translated, with the source language named.

chosen.channel: GO Classes for GATE CS (Deepak Poonia)
chosen.title: Discrete Mathematics, Module 7 Group Theory - the published lecture sequence
covers: lecture 11 classification of binary algebraic structures
lecture 38 alternative definitions of abelian group
chosen.why: The lecture titles are the closest published map of this topic in GATE order, and they were used to check that the subtopic enumeration is complete rather than to source any statement. Recorded as structure only: the video captions could not be retrieved in this run, so no card quotes or timestamps it.

rejected.channel: NPTEL, IIT Madras (Dr. Kamala Krithivasan, Discrete Mathematical Structures)
rejected.title: Lectures 35, 36 and 37 - Algebras
rejected.why: The natural first choice: the same course supplied the full-transcript Lecture 40 that carried the previous topic, and its three 'Algebras' lectures cover exactly this syllabus line. This run could not fetch the transcript PDFs - the host refused the request from the sandbox - so nothing could be read and no claim rests on them. Rejected for access, not for quality; worth retrying in a later run.

rejected.title: Introduction to Abstract Group Theory, lectures 1-40
rejected.why: Covers the topic completely and well beyond it - group actions, Sylow theory, isomorphism theorems, alternating groups - which is the wrong depth for a two-word GATE line, and its captions could not be read in this run either. Rejected on both scope and access.

rejected.title: 1.13 GROUP THEORY (Complete Playlist), 21 videos
rejected.why: A serious Hindi alternative whose video titles map one-to-one onto the ladder (closure, associative, identity, inverse, commutative, order of an element, cyclic group), and the strongest competitor to the Hindi lecture that was chosen. Only its title list could be read in this run; no caption text for any of its videos was retrievable, so it could not supply a single verified sentence. Rejected for access, not for language.

rejected.title: Group Theory, 34 videos
rejected.why: Large, complete and well regarded, but it is an engineering-mathematics sequence that runs on into ring theory and vector spaces, with no GATE question work and no readable captions in this run. The biggest playlist is not automatically the best fit for a two-mark GATE line.

rejected.channel: GateAI / Success Tracker / Testbook / EduRev / BattleExam
rejected.title: Secondary GATE answer sites
rejected.why: Used only to cross-check paper question numbering, never as a source of content: several of these sites disagree with each other (one prints 8 for GATE CSE 2014 Set 3 Q.50 where the accepted answer is 4) and none of them shows its own evidence. Every PYQ answer in this topic is taken from the GATE Overflow discussion page and then recomputed.

rejected.title: Set Theory and Algebra - subject notes
rejected.why: Read and rejected as a teaching source: it is a compressed revision sheet of definitions that assumes the material already, which is the opposite of what a beginner-first card set needs. Its definitions were used only to confirm that the GeeksforGeeks wording is standard.
